  let A : (n : ℕ) → ℝ≥0 → Set (Hist n) := fun n T =>
    {h | (∀ j, ∃ a : ℝ≥0 × (E × E), h j = Sum.inl a) ∧
      StrictMono (fun j => readTime (h j)) ∧
      ∀ i : Fin n, readTime (h i.succ) < (T : ℝ)}
  change ∀ n : ℕ, ∀ T : ℝ≥0, ∀ y xRef : E, ∀ z₀ : E × E,
      let a : Hist n → ℝ := fun h => readTime (h (Fin.last n))
      let append : Hist n × ℝ → Hist (n+1) := fun p =>
        Fin.snoc p.1 (match p.1 (Fin.last n) with
          | Sum.inl r => Sum.inl (r.1 + Real.toNNReal (p.2 - a p.1),
              S xRef (Φ y xRef (p.2 - a p.1) r.2))
          | Sum.inr _ => Sum.inr ())
      let D : Hist n → ℝ → ℝ≥0∞ := fun h u =>
        if a h < u ∧ u < (T : ℝ) then
          match h (Fin.last n) with
          | Sum.inl r => ENNReal.ofReal (rate xRef (Φ y xRef (u - a h) r.2) *
              Real.exp (-Λ y xRef r.2 (Real.toNNReal (u - a h))))
          | Sum.inr _ => 0
        else 0
      ∀ F : Hist (n+1) → ℝ≥0∞, Measurable F →
        let J : Hist n → ℝ≥0∞ := fun h => ∫⁻ u : ℝ, F (append (h,u)) * D h u
        Measurable J ∧
        (∫⁻ w in history y xRef z₀ (n+1) ⁻¹' A (n+1) T,
          F (history y xRef z₀ (n+1) w) ∂P) =
        ∫⁻ w in history y xRef z₀ n ⁻¹' A n T,

  let append : Hist n × ℝ → Hist (n+1) := fun p =>

      | Sum.inl r => Sum.inl (r.1 + Real.toNNReal (p.2 - a p.1),
          S xRef (Φ y xRef (p.2 - a p.1) r.2))
      | Sum.inr _ => Sum.inr ())

      | Sum.inl r => ENNReal.ofReal (rate xRef (Φ y xRef (u - a h) r.2) *
          Real.exp (-Λ y xRef r.2 (Real.toNNReal (u - a h))))

  have hread : readTime = @AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.ProximalBPS.ActualOrderedPrefix.readTime (E × E) := by
    funext r; cases r <;> rfl

  have hid := hloc (A n T) hA

        readTime (record y xRef z₀ (ε w) n) < readTime (record y xRef z₀ (ε w) (n+1)) ∧

    rw [Set.inter_comm]

      F (history y xRef z₀ (n+1) w) ∂P) =

  rw [hevent] at hid

  exact hid.trans (setLIntegral_map (μ := P) hA hJ hHist')

steps.title: Disintegrate the ordered simplex with its actual subtype measure
steps.text: Appending u to s belongs to Δ_(n+1)(T) exactly when s lies in Δ_n(T) and s_n<u<T. Fixed Mathlib proves that inserting the last real coordinate preserves product Lebesgue volume. Pull back the simplex indicator and apply nonnegative Tonelli to obtain the iterated integral. For a Borel function defined only on the simplex subtype, extend it measurably to the ambient finite product using the measurable inclusion. It agrees on the subtype; all integrals are restricted there, so outside values have no effect. The comap integral formula transfers the resulting equality back to the dependent simplex and interval subtypes. The argument includes empty domains and infinite integrals.
steps.lean:
private theorem strictMono_snoc (n : ℕ) (f : Fin (n + 1) → ℝ) (u : ℝ) :
    StrictMono (Fin.snoc f u) ↔ StrictMono f ∧ f (Fin.last n) < u := by
  rw [Fin.strictMono_iff_lt_succ, Fin.forall_iff_castSucc]
  simp only [Fin.succ_castSucc, Fin.snoc_castSucc,
    Fin.snoc_last, Fin.succ_last]
  rw [← Fin.strictMono_iff_lt_succ, and_comm]

private theorem simplex_snoc (n : ℕ) (T : ℝ≥0) (t : Fin n → ℝ) (u : ℝ) :
    (StrictMono (Fin.cons (0 : ℝ) (Fin.snoc t u)) ∧
      ∀ i, (Fin.snoc t u : Fin (n+1) → ℝ) i < (T : ℝ)) ↔
    (StrictMono (Fin.cons (0 : ℝ) t) ∧ ∀ i, t i < (T : ℝ)) ∧
      (Fin.cons (0 : ℝ) t : Fin (n+1) → ℝ) (Fin.last n) < u ∧ u < (T : ℝ) := by
  rw [Fin.cons_snoc_eq_snoc_cons, strictMono_snoc]
  simp only [Fin.forall_iff_castSucc, Fin.snoc_castSucc, Fin.snoc_last]
  tauto

private theorem snoc_volume_preserving (n : ℕ) :
    MeasurePreserving (fun p : ℝ × (Fin n → ℝ) => Fin.snoc p.2 p.1)
      (volume.prod volume) (volume : Measure (Fin (n+1) → ℝ)) := by
  have h := (volume_preserving_piFinSuccAbove (fun _ : Fin (n+1) => ℝ) (Fin.last n)).symm
  change MeasurePreserving (fun p : ℝ × (Fin n → ℝ) =>
    @Fin.insertNth n (fun _ : Fin (n+1) => ℝ) (Fin.last n) p.1 p.2) (volume.prod volume) volume at h
  simpa only [Fin.insertNth_last'] using h

private def orderedSimplex (n : ℕ) (T : ℝ≥0) : Set (Fin n → ℝ) :=
  {t | StrictMono (Fin.cons (0 : ℝ) t) ∧ ∀ i, t i < (T : ℝ)}

private theorem simplex_lintegral_snoc (n : ℕ) (T : ℝ≥0)
    (hn : MeasurableSet (orderedSimplex n T)) (hs : MeasurableSet (orderedSimplex (n+1) T))
    (F : (Fin (n+1) → ℝ) → ℝ≥0∞) (hF : Measurable F) :
    (∫⁻ t in orderedSimplex (n+1) T, F t) =
      ∫⁻ t in orderedSimplex n T, ∫⁻ u in Set.Ioo
        ((Fin.cons (0 : ℝ) t : Fin (n+1) → ℝ) (Fin.last n)) (T : ℝ),
        F (Fin.snoc t u) := by
  let G : (Fin (n+1) → ℝ) → ℝ≥0∞ := (orderedSimplex (n+1) T).indicator F
  have hg : Measurable G := hF.indicator hs
  have hcomp := (snoc_volume_preserving n).lintegral_comp hg
  rw [lintegral_indicator hs] at hcomp
  rw [← hcomp]
  rw [lintegral_prod_symm (μ := volume) (ν := volume)
    (fun p : ℝ × (Fin n → ℝ) => G (Fin.snoc p.2 p.1))
    (hg.comp (snoc_volume_preserving n).measurable).aemeasurable]
  rw [← lintegral_indicator hn]
  apply lintegral_congr
  intro t
  by_cases ht : t ∈ orderedSimplex n T
  · rw [Set.indicator_of_mem ht, ← lintegral_indicator measurableSet_Ioo]
    apply lintegral_congr
    intro u
    have he : (Fin.snoc t u : Fin (n+1) → ℝ) ∈ orderedSimplex (n+1) T ↔
        ((Fin.cons (0 : ℝ) t : Fin (n+1) → ℝ) (Fin.last n) < u ∧ u < (T : ℝ)) := by
      change (StrictMono (Fin.cons (0 : ℝ) (Fin.snoc t u)) ∧
        ∀ i, (Fin.snoc t u : Fin (n+1) → ℝ) i < (T : ℝ)) ↔ _
      rw [simplex_snoc]
      exact and_iff_right ht
    change (orderedSimplex (n+1) T).indicator F (Fin.snoc t u) =
      (Set.Ioo ((Fin.cons (0 : ℝ) t : Fin (n+1) → ℝ) (Fin.last n)) (T : ℝ)).indicator
        (fun u => F (Fin.snoc t u)) u
    by_cases hu : (Fin.cons (0 : ℝ) t : Fin (n+1) → ℝ) (Fin.last n) < u ∧ u < (T : ℝ)
    · rw [Set.indicator_of_mem (he.mpr hu), Set.indicator_of_mem (s := Set.Ioo ((Fin.cons (0 : ℝ) t : Fin (n+1) → ℝ) (Fin.last n)) (T : ℝ)) hu]
    · rw [Set.indicator_of_notMem (fun h => hu (he.mp h)), Set.indicator_of_notMem (s := Set.Ioo ((Fin.cons (0 : ℝ) t : Fin (n+1) → ℝ) (Fin.last n)) (T : ℝ)) hu]
  · rw [Set.indicator_of_notMem ht]
    have hz : ∀ u : ℝ, G (Fin.snoc t u) = 0 := by
      intro u
      apply Set.indicator_of_notMem
      intro h
      exact ht ((simplex_snoc n T t u).mp h).1
    simp only [hz, lintegral_zero]


private def snocPrefix (n : ℕ) (T : ℝ≥0) (t : orderedSimplex n T)
    (u : Set.Ioo ((Fin.cons (0 : ℝ) t.val : Fin (n+1) → ℝ) (Fin.last n)) (T : ℝ)) :
    orderedSimplex (n+1) T :=
  ⟨Fin.snoc t.val u.val, (simplex_snoc n T t.val u.val).mpr ⟨t.property, u.property⟩⟩

private theorem subtype_simplex_lintegral_snoc (n : ℕ) (T : ℝ≥0)
    (hn : MeasurableSet (orderedSimplex n T)) (hs : MeasurableSet (orderedSimplex (n+1) T))
    (F : orderedSimplex (n+1) T → ℝ≥0∞) (hF : Measurable F) :
    (∫⁻ t : orderedSimplex (n+1) T, F t ∂(volume.comap Subtype.val)) =
      ∫⁻ t : orderedSimplex n T,
        ∫⁻ u : Set.Ioo ((Fin.cons (0 : ℝ) t.val : Fin (n+1) → ℝ) (Fin.last n)) (T : ℝ),
          F (snocPrefix n T t u) ∂(volume.comap Subtype.val)
        ∂(volume.comap Subtype.val) := by
  obtain ⟨G, hG, hext⟩ := (MeasurableEmbedding.subtype_coe hs).exists_measurable_extend hF
    (fun _ => inferInstance)
  have he (t : orderedSimplex (n+1) T) : G t.val = F t := congrFun hext t
  calc
    (∫⁻ t : orderedSimplex (n+1) T, F t ∂(volume.comap Subtype.val)) =
        ∫⁻ t : orderedSimplex (n+1) T, G t.val ∂(volume.comap Subtype.val) :=
      lintegral_congr fun t => (he t).symm
    _ = ∫⁻ t in orderedSimplex (n+1) T, G t := lintegral_subtype_comap hs G
    _ = ∫⁻ t in orderedSimplex n T,
        ∫⁻ u in Set.Ioo ((Fin.cons (0 : ℝ) t : Fin (n+1) → ℝ) (Fin.last n)) (T : ℝ),
          G (Fin.snoc t u) := simplex_lintegral_snoc n T hn hs G hG
    _ = ∫⁻ t : orderedSimplex n T,
        (∫⁻ u in Set.Ioo ((Fin.cons (0 : ℝ) t.val : Fin (n+1) → ℝ) (Fin.last n)) (T : ℝ),
          G (Fin.snoc t.val u)) ∂(volume.comap Subtype.val) :=
      (lintegral_subtype_comap hn _).symm
    _ = _ := by
      apply lintegral_congr
      intro t
      rw [← lintegral_subtype_comap measurableSet_Ioo (fun u => G (Fin.snoc t.val u))]
      apply lintegral_congr
      intro u
      exact he (snocPrefix n T t u)

steps.title: Identify the appended history and factor the density
steps.text: Finite induction shows that appending a last time leaves every earlier state unchanged and adds state S_rΦ_(u−s_n)z_n. Since s_n≥0 and u>s_n, toNNReal(s_n)+toNNReal(u−s_n)=toNNReal(u); therefore absolute append equals K_(n+1)(s,u) as a complete history. Split the finite product at its last index to get q_(n+1)=q_n times the next pre-bounce rate and elapsed survival. The real product is already nonnegative, so ofReal preserves this multiplication. These private algebraic inputs are instantiated by the actual flow, reflection, rate and hazard in the induction.
steps.lean:
private def state {Z : Type*} (step : ℝ → Z → Z) (z₀ : Z) (n : ℕ) (t : Fin n → ℝ) :
    Fin (n+1) → Z :=
  Fin.induction z₀ (fun i z => step
    (t i - (Fin.cons (0 : ℝ) t : Fin (n+1) → ℝ) i.castSucc) z)

private theorem state_snoc_prefix {Z : Type*} (step : ℝ → Z → Z) (z₀ : Z)
    (n : ℕ) (t : Fin n → ℝ) (u : ℝ) (j : Fin (n+1)) :
    state step z₀ (n+1) (Fin.snoc t u) j.castSucc = state step z₀ n t j := by
  induction j using Fin.induction with
  | zero => rfl
  | succ i ih =>
    rw [← Fin.succ_castSucc]
    change step ((Fin.snoc t u : Fin (n+1) → ℝ) i.castSucc -
      (Fin.cons (0 : ℝ) (Fin.snoc t u) : Fin (n+2) → ℝ) i.castSucc.castSucc)
      (state step z₀ (n+1) (Fin.snoc t u) i.castSucc.castSucc) =
      step (t i - (Fin.cons (0 : ℝ) t : Fin (n+1) → ℝ) i.castSucc)
        (state step z₀ n t i.castSucc)
    rw [ih, Fin.snoc_castSucc, Fin.cons_snoc_eq_snoc_cons, Fin.snoc_castSucc]

private theorem state_snoc_last {Z : Type*} (step : ℝ → Z → Z) (z₀ : Z)
    (n : ℕ) (t : Fin n → ℝ) (u : ℝ) :
    state step z₀ (n+1) (Fin.snoc t u) (Fin.last (n+1)) =
      step (u - (Fin.cons (0 : ℝ) t : Fin (n+1) → ℝ) (Fin.last n))
        (state step z₀ n t (Fin.last n)) := by
  rw [show Fin.last (n+1) = (Fin.last n).succ from rfl]
  change step ((Fin.snoc t u : Fin (n+1) → ℝ) (Fin.last n) -
    (Fin.cons (0 : ℝ) (Fin.snoc t u) : Fin (n+2) → ℝ) (Fin.last n).castSucc)
    (state step z₀ (n+1) (Fin.snoc t u) (Fin.last n).castSucc) = _
  rw [Fin.snoc_last, Fin.cons_snoc_eq_snoc_cons, Fin.snoc_castSucc, state_snoc_prefix]

private def weight {Z : Type*} (step : ℝ → Z → Z) (factor : Z → ℝ → ℝ)
    (z₀ : Z) (n : ℕ) (t : Fin n → ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ∏ i : Fin n, factor (state step z₀ n t i.castSucc)
    (t i - (Fin.cons (0 : ℝ) t : Fin (n+1) → ℝ) i.castSucc)

private theorem weight_snoc {Z : Type*} (step : ℝ → Z → Z) (factor : Z → ℝ → ℝ)
    (z₀ : Z) (n : ℕ) (t : Fin n → ℝ) (u : ℝ) :
    weight step factor z₀ (n+1) (Fin.snoc t u) = weight step factor z₀ n t *
      factor (state step z₀ n t (Fin.last n))
        (u - (Fin.cons (0 : ℝ) t : Fin (n+1) → ℝ) (Fin.last n)) := by
  simp only [weight, Fin.prod_univ_castSucc]
  rw [state_snoc_prefix, Fin.snoc_last, Fin.cons_snoc_eq_snoc_cons, Fin.snoc_castSucc]
  congr 1
  apply Finset.prod_congr rfl
  intro i _
  simp only [state_snoc_prefix, Fin.snoc_castSucc]


private def timedHistory {Z : Type*} (step : ℝ → Z → Z) (z₀ : Z)
    (n : ℕ) (t : Fin n → ℝ) : Fin (n+1) → ((ℝ≥0 × Z) ⊕ Unit) :=
  fun j => Sum.inl (Real.toNNReal ((Fin.cons (0 : ℝ) t : Fin (n+1) → ℝ) j),
    state step z₀ n t j)

private theorem timedHistory_snoc {Z : Type*} (step : ℝ → Z → Z) (z₀ : Z)
    (n : ℕ) (t : Fin n → ℝ) (u : ℝ)
    (ht : 0 ≤ (Fin.cons (0 : ℝ) t : Fin (n+1) → ℝ) (Fin.last n))
    (hu : (Fin.cons (0 : ℝ) t : Fin (n+1) → ℝ) (Fin.last n) ≤ u) :
    timedHistory step z₀ (n+1) (Fin.snoc t u) =
      Fin.snoc (timedHistory step z₀ n t)
        (Sum.inl (Real.toNNReal ((Fin.cons (0 : ℝ) t : Fin (n+1) → ℝ) (Fin.last n)) +
          Real.toNNReal (u - (Fin.cons (0 : ℝ) t : Fin (n+1) → ℝ) (Fin.last n)),
          step (u - (Fin.cons (0 : ℝ) t : Fin (n+1) → ℝ) (Fin.last n))
            (state step z₀ n t (Fin.last n)))) := by
  funext j
  induction j using Fin.lastCases with
  | last =>
    simp only [timedHistory, Fin.snoc_last, Fin.cons_snoc_eq_snoc_cons, state_snoc_last]
    congr 2
    apply NNReal.eq
    simp only [NNReal.coe_add, Real.coe_toNNReal _ ht,
      Real.coe_toNNReal _ (sub_nonneg.mpr hu), Real.coe_toNNReal _ (ht.trans hu)]
    ring
  | cast i =>
    simp only [timedHistory, Fin.snoc_castSucc, Fin.cons_snoc_eq_snoc_cons,
      state_snoc_prefix]

private theorem ordered_last_nonneg (n : ℕ) (t : Fin n → ℝ)
    (ht : StrictMono (Fin.cons (0 : ℝ) t)) :
    0 ≤ (Fin.cons (0 : ℝ) t : Fin (n+1) → ℝ) (Fin.last n) := by
  have h := ht.monotone (Fin.zero_le (Fin.last n))
  simpa only [Fin.cons_zero] using h

private theorem weight_snoc_ofReal {Z : Type*} (step : ℝ → Z → Z)
    (factor : Z → ℝ → ℝ) (z₀ : Z) (n : ℕ) (t : Fin n → ℝ) (u : ℝ)
    (hweight : 0 ≤ weight step factor z₀ n t) :
    ENNReal.ofReal (weight step factor z₀ (n+1) (Fin.snoc t u)) =
      ENNReal.ofReal (weight step factor z₀ n t) *
      ENNReal.ofReal (factor (state step z₀ n t (Fin.last n))
        (u - (Fin.cons (0 : ℝ) t : Fin (n+1) → ℝ) (Fin.last n))) := by
  rw [weight_snoc, ENNReal.ofReal_mul hweight]

steps.title: Close the all-n probability induction for every nonnegative test
steps.text: Assume the test identity at n. Apply it to the Borel J_F produced by the actual recurrence. The resulting integrand is J_F(K_n(s))q_n(s). At K_n(s), the next-event density is the indicator of s_n<u<T times ρ(z_n,u−s_n). Move the finite nonnegative scalar q_n(s)=ofReal(qReal_n(s)) inside the nonnegative integral, restrict to that open interval, and use the exact append and product identities. The result is F(K_(n+1)(s,u))q_(n+1)(s,u). The subtype Tonelli equality turns the two integrals into the integral over Δ_(n+1). Joint Borel K and q ensure the composed test is Borel. Together with the zero-event base this proves the formula for every n, without boundedness or integrability.

steps.title: Recover the measure equality and the exact missing mass
steps.text: Compare both pushforward measures against every Borel ENNReal test. The map-integral formula and the withDensity formula turn their integrals into the identity just proved; measure extensionality gives equality. Taking F=1 gives ∫q_n dm_n=P(B_n(T)), and the canonical probability normalization gives P(B_n(T))≤1. This mass is not renormalized. The private all-test input is supplied by the actual all-n induction, not by a public hypothesis.

    [MeasurableSpace Ω] [MeasurableSpace X] [MeasurableSpace H]
    (P : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure P] (m : Measure X)
    (B : Set Ω) (history : Ω → H) (K : X → H) (q : X → ℝ≥0∞)
    (hH : Measurable history) (hK : Measurable K) (hq : Measurable q)
    (htest : ∀ F : H → ℝ≥0∞, Measurable F →
      (∫⁻ w in B, F (history w) ∂P) = ∫⁻ t, F (K t) * q t ∂m) :
    Measure.map history (P.restrict B) = Measure.map K (m.withDensity q) ∧
      (∫⁻ t, q t ∂m) = P B ∧ P B ≤ 1 := by
  refine ⟨?_, ?_, prob_le_one⟩
  · apply Measure.ext_of_lintegral
    intro F hF
    rw [lintegral_map hF hH, lintegral_map hF hK,
      lintegral_withDensity_eq_lintegral_mul m hq (g := fun t => F (K t)) (hF.comp hK)]
    exact (htest F hF).trans (lintegral_congr fun _ => mul_comm _ _)
  · have h := htest (fun _ => 1) measurable_const
    simpa only [one_mul, lintegral_const, Measure.restrict_apply MeasurableSet.univ,
      Set.univ_inter] using h.symm

  let Λ : E → E → (E × E) → ℝ≥0 → ℝ := fun y xRef z t =>
    ∫ s in (0 : ℝ)..(t : ℝ), rate xRef (Φ y xRef s z)
  let τ : E → E → (E × E) → ℝ≥0 → WithTop ℝ≥0 := fun y xRef z e =>
    MeasureTheory.hittingAfter
      (fun t : ℝ≥0 => fun a : (E × E) × (E × E) × ℝ≥0 =>
        Λ a.1.1 a.1.2 a.2.1 t - (a.2.2 : ℝ))
      (Set.Ici (0 : ℝ)) 0 ((y, xRef), z, e)
  let next : E → E → ℝ≥0 → ((ℝ≥0 × (E × E)) ⊕ Unit) →
      ((ℝ≥0 × (E × E)) ⊕ Unit) := fun y xRef e r =>
    match r with
    | Sum.inr _ => Sum.inr ()
    | Sum.inl a =>
      if τ y xRef a.2 e = ⊤ then Sum.inr () else
        Sum.inl (a.1 + (τ y xRef a.2 e).untopD 0,
          S xRef (Φ y xRef (((τ y xRef a.2 e).untopD 0 : ℝ≥0) : ℝ) a.2))
  let record : E → E → (E × E) → (ℕ → ℝ≥0) → ℕ →
      ((ℝ≥0 × (E × E)) ⊕ Unit) := fun y xRef z₀ e n =>
    Nat.rec (Sum.inl (0, z₀)) (fun k r => next y xRef (e k) r) n
  let P : Measure (ℕ → ℝ) := Measure.infinitePi (fun _ : ℕ => expMeasure (1 : ℝ))
  let ε : (ℕ → ℝ) → ℕ → ℝ≥0 := fun w k => Real.toNNReal (w k)
  let history : E → E → (E × E) → (n : ℕ) → (ℕ → ℝ) →
      (Fin (n + 1) → ((ℝ≥0 × (E × E)) ⊕ Unit)) :=
    fun y xRef z₀ n w j => record y xRef z₀ (ε w) j.val
  let Rec := (ℝ≥0 × (E × E)) ⊕ Unit
  let Hist : ℕ → Type _ := fun n => Fin (n + 1) → Rec
  let readTime : Rec → ℝ := fun r => match r with
    | Sum.inl q => (q.1 : ℝ)
    | Sum.inr _ => 0
  let Δ : (n : ℕ) → ℝ≥0 → Set (Fin n → ℝ) := fun n T =>
    {t | StrictMono (Fin.cons (0 : ℝ) t) ∧ ∀ i, t i < (T : ℝ)}
  let Prefix : (n : ℕ) → ℝ≥0 → Type := fun n T => {t : Fin n → ℝ // t ∈ Δ n T}
  let m : (n : ℕ) → (T : ℝ≥0) → Measure (Prefix n T) := fun n T =>
    Measure.comap (fun t : Prefix n T => t.val) (volume : Measure (Fin n → ℝ))
  let zAt : E → E → (E × E) → (n : ℕ) → (T : ℝ≥0) →
      Prefix n T → Fin (n + 1) → (E × E) := fun y xRef z₀ n T t =>
    Fin.induction z₀ (fun i z =>
      S xRef (Φ y xRef (t.val i - (Fin.cons (0 : ℝ) (t.val : Fin n → ℝ) : Fin (n + 1) → ℝ) i.castSucc) z))
  let K : E → E → (E × E) → (n : ℕ) → (T : ℝ≥0) →
      Prefix n T → Hist n := fun y xRef z₀ n T t j =>
    Sum.inl (Real.toNNReal ((Fin.cons (0 : ℝ) (t.val : Fin n → ℝ) : Fin (n + 1) → ℝ) j), zAt y xRef z₀ n T t j)
  let qReal : E → E → (E × E) → (n : ℕ) → (T : ℝ≥0) →
      Prefix n T → ℝ := fun y xRef z₀ n T t =>
    ∏ i : Fin n,
      rate xRef (Φ y xRef (t.val i - (Fin.cons (0 : ℝ) (t.val : Fin n → ℝ) : Fin (n + 1) → ℝ) i.castSucc)
        (zAt y xRef z₀ n T t i.castSucc)) *
      Real.exp (-Λ y xRef (zAt y xRef z₀ n T t i.castSucc)
        (Real.toNNReal (t.val i - (Fin.cons (0 : ℝ) (t.val : Fin n → ℝ) : Fin (n + 1) → ℝ) i.castSucc)))
  let q : E → E → (E × E) → (n : ℕ) → (T : ℝ≥0) →
      Prefix n T → ℝ≥0∞ := fun y xRef z₀ n T t =>
    ENNReal.ofReal (qReal y xRef z₀ n T t)
  let A : (n : ℕ) → ℝ≥0 → Set (Hist n) := fun n T =>
    {h | (∀ j, ∃ a : ℝ≥0 × (E × E), h j = Sum.inl a) ∧
      StrictMono (fun j => readTime (h j)) ∧
      ∀ i : Fin n, readTime (h i.succ) < (T : ℝ)}
  change ∀ n : ℕ, ∀ T : ℝ≥0,
      MeasurableSet (Δ n T) ∧ MeasurableSet (A n T) ∧
      Measurable (fun p : ((E × E) × (E × E)) × Prefix n T =>
        K p.1.1.1 p.1.1.2 p.1.2 n T p.2) ∧
      Measurable (fun p : ((E × E) × (E × E)) × Prefix n T =>
        q p.1.1.1 p.1.1.2 p.1.2 n T p.2) ∧
      (∀ y xRef : E, ∀ z₀ : E × E,
        let H : (ℕ → ℝ) → Hist n := history y xRef z₀ n
        let B : Set (ℕ → ℝ) := H ⁻¹' A n T
        let obs : (ℕ → ℝ) → Fin n → ℝ := fun w i => readTime (H w i.succ)
        Measurable H ∧ MeasurableSet B ∧ Measurable obs ∧
        (∀ t : Prefix n T, 0 ≤ qReal y xRef z₀ n T t) ∧
        (∀ w ∈ B, ∃ t : Prefix n T, t.val = obs w ∧ H w = K y xRef z₀ n T t) ∧
        Measure.map H (P.restrict B) =
          Measure.map (K y xRef z₀ n T) ((m n T).withDensity (q y xRef z₀ n T)) ∧
        (∀ F : Hist n → ℝ≥0∞, Measurable F →
          (∫⁻ w in B, F (H w) ∂P) =
            ∫⁻ t : Prefix n T, F (K y xRef z₀ n T t) * q y xRef z₀ n T t ∂m n T) ∧
        (∫⁻ t : Prefix n T, q y xRef z₀ n T t ∂m n T) = P B ∧
        P B ≤ 1)
  intro n T
  have hg := ordered_prefix_borel_data hα hαβ hV hH hη hβη n T
  refine ⟨hg.1, hg.2.1, hg.2.2.1, hg.2.2.2.1, ?_⟩
  intro y xRef z₀
  dsimp only
  have h91 := AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.ProximalBPS.ActualAbsoluteNextEventTime.actual_absolute_next_event_time_law
    hα hαβ hV hH hη hβη y xRef z₀ n
  have hHist : Measurable (history y xRef z₀ n) := h91.1
  have hB : MeasurableSet (history y xRef z₀ n ⁻¹' A n T) := hg.2.1.preimage hHist
  have hread : readTime = @AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.ProximalBPS.ActualOrderedPrefix.readTime (E × E) := by
    funext r; cases r <;> rfl
  have hObs : Measurable (fun w : ℕ → ℝ => fun i : Fin n =>
      readTime (history y xRef z₀ n w i.succ)) := by
    rw [hread]
    apply measurable_pi_lambda
    intro i
    exact readTime_measurable.comp ((measurable_pi_apply i.succ).comp hHist)
  have hparams : Measurable (fun t : Prefix n T => (((y, xRef), z₀), t)) :=
    measurable_const.prodMk measurable_id
  have hKjoint : Measurable (fun p : ((E × E) × (E × E)) × Prefix n T =>
      K p.1.1.1 p.1.1.2 p.1.2 n T p.2) := hg.2.2.1
  have hqjoint : Measurable (fun p : ((E × E) × (E × E)) × Prefix n T =>
      q p.1.1.1 p.1.1.2 p.1.2 n T p.2) := hg.2.2.2.1
  have hK := hKjoint.comp hparams
  have hq := hqjoint.comp hparams
  dsimp only [Function.comp_def] at hK hq
  have htest := actual_prefix_all_integrals hα hαβ hV hH hη hβη n T y xRef z₀
  letI : IsProbabilityMeasure P :=
    AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Probability.UnitExponentialProduct.unit_exponential_product_laws.1
  have hclosure := law_and_mass_of_all_tests P (m n T)
    (history y xRef z₀ n ⁻¹' A n T) (history y xRef z₀ n)
    (K y xRef z₀ n T) (q y xRef z₀ n T) hHist hK hq htest
  refine ⟨hHist, hB, hObs, hg.2.2.2.2 y xRef z₀, ?_, hclosure.1, htest,
    hclosure.2.1, hclosure.2.2⟩
  exact actual_prefix_identification hα hαβ hV hH hη hβη n T y xRef z₀

lesson.lean_statement: Let E be any finite-dimensional real inner-product Borel space, including dimension zero. Let V:E→ℝ be C², α,β≥0 and η∈ℝ with α>0, α≤β, α‖v‖²≤D²V(x)[v,v]≤β‖v‖² for every x,v∈E, η>0 and βη≤1. Fix any deterministic y,r∈E and initial phase z₀∈E×E. Put c=y−η∇V(r), Φ_t(x,p)=(c+cos(t)(x−c)+√η sin(t)p, −sin(t)(x−c)/√η+cos(t)p), g_r(x)=∇V(x)−∇V(r), S_r(x,p)=(x,p−2〈p,g_r(x)〉g_r(x)/‖g_r(x)‖²), λ_r(x,p)=√η max{0,〈p,g_r(x)〉}, Λ_z(t)=∫₀ᵗλ_r(Φ_s(z))ds and τ_z(e)=inf{t≥0:Λ_z(t)≥e}∈[0,∞], with inf empty=∞. Total real division makes S_r the identity at g_r(x)=0. The record space is D=([0,∞)×(E×E))⊕{stopped}, with Borel sum structure. Define next(e,stopped)=stopped; for a live record (T,z), next(e,(T,z))=stopped if τ_z(e)=∞, and otherwise next(e,(T,z))=(T+τ_z(e),S_rΦ_(τ_z(e))(z)). In the Lean definition untopD0 is used only in this non-top branch. Define R₀(e)=live(0,z₀) and R_(j+1)(e)=next(e_j,R_j(e)). Let Ω=ℝ^ℕ with its product Borel structure and P=⊗_(k≥0)Exp(1). Let ε(w)_k=max{w_k,0}; this is an ambient coordinate extension on a P-null nonpositive-clock set, not new source dynamics for negative clocks. For every deterministic finite n≥0 and finite horizon T≥0, let Hist_n=D^(Fin(n+1)) and H_n(w)=(R_j(ε(w)))_(0≤j≤n). Write rtime(live(a,z))=a and rtime(stopped)=0. Define the measurable ordered simplex Δ_n(T)={t∈ℝ^n:0<t_1<⋯<t_n<T}; its subtype carries m_n, the comap of product Lebesgue volume along inclusion. For t∈Δ_n(T), put s_0=0,s_i=t_i, z_0=z₀ and z_i=S_rΦ_(s_i−s_(i−1))(z_(i−1)) for 1≤i≤n. Define K_n(t)_j=live(s_j,z_j). Define qReal_n(t)=∏_(i=1)^n [λ_r(Φ_(s_i−s_(i−1))(z_(i−1))) exp(−Λ_(z_(i−1))(s_i−s_(i−1)))] and q_n=ofReal(qReal_n). Here the literal Lean definitions use toNNReal on times and elapsed times; these agree with the displayed nonnegative values on the simplex. Let A_n(T) be the abstract-history set in which all n+1 records are live, their read times are strictly increasing, and each postinitial read time is below T. A_n(T) does not itself constrain the initial record time. Set B_n(T)=H_n^(-1)(A_n(T)) and obs_n(w)_i=rtime(H_n(w)_(i+1)); actual H_n(w)_0 is always live(0,z₀). Then Δ_n(T) and A_n(T) are Borel. For fixed n,T, K_n and q_n are jointly Borel in (y,r,z₀,t). For every y,r,z₀, H_n,obs_n and B_n(T) are Borel, and qReal_n(t)≥0 for every simplex point. For every raw w∈B_n(T), there exists t∈Δ_n(T) with t=obs_n(w) and H_n(w)=K_n(t), as complete tagged histories. The exact unnormalized law is (H_n)_*(P restricted to B_n(T))=(K_n)_*(q_n m_n). For every Borel F:Hist_n→[0,∞], ∫_(B_n(T))F(H_n(w))P(dw)=∫_(Δ_n(T))F(K_n(t))q_n(t)m_n(dt). Moreover ∫q_n dm_n=P(B_n(T))≤1. This includes n=0,T=0, zero hazard and extended-valued tests; there is no boundedness, integrability or positive-event-mass assumption. This is the strict first-n-prefix law, without a final survival factor, and is not a raw exact-n event-count law. It is an attributed ASTIS completion of the finite ordered iteration ingredient implicit in Appendix A.1(A.7), with joint Borel construction from Appendix A.2. The dimension-zero and ENNReal-test extensions are explicit ASTIS extensions. Terminal survival, endpoint/count identification, the full path-functional A.7 expansion, restart/Markovness, invariance, hypocoercivity, implementation errors, expected costs and full paper/composition remain outside this result.

reconstruction.text:
# Independent anonymous Lean reconstruction

Only the supplied anonymous statement, approved mathematical definition context, and packet metadata were read. No source theorem text, source anchor, original Lean declaration, previous audit or repair was consulted. This is a reconstruction, not a source-fidelity verdict. The packet reports compiled=true; no proof or independent Lean build was inspected.

## Objects, domains and hypotheses

Let E be any finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its normed additive group structure and Borel measurable structure, including dimension zero. Let V:E→R be twice continuously Frechet differentiable, α,β be nonnegative real numbers, and η be real. Assume

    0<α,   α≤β,   0<η,   βη≤1,
    α||v||² ≤ D²V(x)[v,v] ≤ β||v||²    for every x,v∈E.

The Hessian here is the displayed iterated Frechet derivative. Write ∇V for the inner-product gradient. There are no higher-derivative hypotheses or additional smoothness constants. Fix arbitrary y,r∈E and z₀=(x₀,v₀)∈E×E. The reference r need not equal x₀. None of y,r,z₀ is random under the input law below.

## All deterministic lets

Define the center c(y,r)=y−η∇V(r). For z=(x,v) and any real s, the flow is

    Φ(y,r,s,z)=(
      c(y,r)+cos(s)(x−c(y,r))+sqrt(η)sin(s)v,
      −sin(s)/sqrt(η)(x−c(y,r))+cos(s)v).

Write g_r(x)=∇V(x)−∇V(r). The reflection map and rate are

    S(r,(x,v))=(x,v−[2〈v,g_r(x)〉/||g_r(x)||²]g_r(x)),
    λ_r(x,v)=sqrt(η)max(0,〈v,g_r(x)〉).

Real division is total, with zero denominator giving quotient zero. In particular S is defined also at g_r(x)=0 and then fixes the state. No nonzero-normal assumption is implicit. The rate is a finite nonnegative real.

For u≥0 define the cumulative hazard

    Λ(y,r,z,u)=∫₀ᵘ λ_r(Φ(y,r,s,z)) ds.

This is the displayed real interval integral. For e≥0 define the extended nonnegative waiting time

    τ(y,r,z,e)=inf{u≥0 : Λ(y,r,z,u)−e≥0},

with infinity if this set is empty. This is exactly hittingAfter with starting time 0 and target [0,∞), using a weak crossing inequality. In particular e=0 gives τ=0. It is a hitting-time definition from the deterministic integrated hazard, not a newly postulated probability law for a waiting time.

Let Rec=([0,∞)×(E×E)) ⊔ {†}, where † denotes the distinct singleton second summand. For a live record (a,z), define next(y,r,e,(a,z)) by first evaluating τ(y,r,z,e). If it is infinity, the result is †; otherwise the result is

    (a+τ, S(r,Φ(y,r,τ,z))).

The map next sends † to †. The explicit comparison τ=∞ occurs BEFORE extracting its value with untopD 0, so the default zero is never used to turn an infinite waiting time into a live event. Flow precedes reflection, and the recorded state is post-reflection. The duration τ is relative; a+τ is an absolute time. There is no test against T in next.

For every nonnegative sequence e:N→[0,∞), the let-bound record is finite recursion:

    record(y,r,z₀,e,0)=(0,z₀),
    record(y,r,z₀,e,k+1)=next(y,r,e(k),record(y,r,z₀,e,k)).

These are finite indexed records, not a supplied global nonexplosive process. Each live step tests only whether its waiting time is infinite, and the cemetery tag is absorbing thereafter.

## Actual random inputs and marked history

Let Ω=R^N and P be the countable product of rate-one exponential measures on R. Under P the coordinate variables w(k) are independent Exp(1) variables. Set ε(w,k)=Real.toNNReal(w(k))=max(w(k),0), represented as a nonnegative real. This defines ε on all of Ω, including points off the support of P; it agrees with the coordinates almost surely.

For every n∈N, let Hist(n)=Rec^{0,...,n}. The let-bound history is

    H(w)(j)=record(y,r,z₀,ε(w),j),    0≤j≤n.

It includes the fixed initial record (0,z₀). It uses exactly the first n input coordinates w(0),...,w(n−1); subsequent coordinates do not affect H. No random initial state, random reference or extra reflection randomness is included. The let-bound readTime sends a live record (a,z) to a as a real and sends † to 0.

## Time-prefix domain, comap measure and reconstruction lets

Fix n∈N and T≥0. The let-bound Δ(n,T)⊂R^n is the set of tuples t=(t₁,...,t_n) with

    0=t₀<t₁<...<t_n<T.

Precisely, StrictMono is applied after prepending 0, and all of the n supplied coordinates must be below T. When n=0 these conditions are vacuous. Prefix(n,T) is the subtype of R^n consisting of Δ(n,T).

The let-bound m(n,T) is Measure.comap along the subtype inclusion of real product Lebesgue volume. It is the unnormalized measure on that measurable subtype: pushing it forward through the inclusion gives Lebesgue measure restricted to Δ(n,T). It is not a normalized uniform probability law. For n=0 the empty-coordinate space and Prefix are singletons, with volume one. For n≥1 and T=0 the subtype is empty.

For t∈Prefix(n,T), put t₀=0 and define the let-bound zAt by

    z_i=S(r,Φ(y,r,t_i−t_{i−1},z_{i−1})),    i=1,...,n,

starting from the given z₀. In the displayed Fin.induction, i.castSucc indexes the old state and old time in the tuple with zero prepended. All these durations are strictly positive. The let-bound history reconstruction K is

    K(y,r,z₀,n,T,t)(j)=(t_j,z_j),    j=0,...,n,

with the live tag at every index. Formally the times are converted by Real.toNNReal; it leaves the times unchanged on this subtype. K records the initial and all post-reflection states, not just event times.

The real density let is

    qReal(y,r,z₀,n,T,t)
      = product over i=1,...,n of
        λ_r(Φ(y,r,t_i−t_{i−1},z_{i−1}))
        × exp(−Λ(y,r,z_{i−1},t_i−t_{i−1})).

The event rate is evaluated BEFORE the reflection at the end of its segment, whereas the starting state z_{i−1} is the previous POST-reflection state. The Real.toNNReal used in the integral's duration leaves it unchanged. The let q is ENNReal.ofReal(qReal), the embedding of max(qReal,0) into [0,∞]. The theorem explicitly asserts qReal≥0 on Prefix. Each density value is finite, since qReal is a finite real product. An empty product is one.

There is no terminal survival factor exp(−Λ(y,r,z_n,T−t_n)). There is also no state flowed forward from t_n to T and no (n+1)-st waiting time in K or q. T appears in the admissible subtype/domain, not as a final evolution segment.

## Accepted history event and full theorem

The let A(n,T)⊂Hist(n) consists of histories h such that:

- Every coordinate is live: for each j, h(j) is some tagged (a,z).
- j↦readTime(h(j)) is strictly increasing.
- readTime(h(i))<T for i=1,...,n.

On the whole Hist(n), A itself does not impose h(0)=(0,z₀), an initial time of zero, consistency of states with Φ or S, or a terminal survival condition. H and K impose their own initial and dynamic conditions. Requiring all tags to be live prevents the readTime(†)=0 convention from admitting cemetery histories.

The theorem is universally quantified over all n∈N and T≥0 and asserts all of the following.

1. Δ(n,T) and A(n,T) are measurable sets.

2. K and q are jointly Borel measurable in (y,r,z₀,t), with domain ((E×E)×(E×E))×Prefix(n,T). The first component is ((y,r),z₀). This is joint measurability, not merely separate measurability with parameters fixed.

3. For every y,r∈E and z₀∈E×E, let H be the actual random history above, B=H^{-1}(A(n,T)), and

       obs(w)=(readTime(H(w)(1)),...,readTime(H(w)(n))).

   Then H and obs are measurable and B is a measurable subset of Ω. Also qReal(t)≥0 for every t∈Prefix(n,T).

4. For every w∈B there exists t∈Prefix(n,T) with t.val=obs(w) and H(w)=K(t). This is pointwise on B, not merely an almost-sure assertion. The statement explicitly asks for existence; equality of the underlying tuple also forces uniqueness in this subtype.

5. As measures on the full tagged marked-history space Hist(n),

       H_*(P restricted to B) = K_*(m(n,T) with density q).

   These are unnormalized measures. In particular P restricted to B is not the conditional probability law given B.

6. For every measurable F:Hist(n)→[0,∞],

       ∫_B F(H(w)) dP(w)
         = ∫_{Prefix(n,T)} F(K(t)) q(t) dm(n,T)(t).

   This is equality of extended nonnegative Lebesgue integrals. F may take infinity; there is no integrability or boundedness premise. A signed-real expectation identity for arbitrary real F is not the displayed claim.

7. The total mass is exactly

       ∫_{Prefix(n,T)} q(t) dm(n,T)(t)=P(B),    P(B)≤1.

   Thus the density describes a subprobability mass, not automatically a probability density with integral one. The theorem does not assert P(B)>0 for all states and parameters.

## Meaning of the prefix and boundary cases

For n≥1, B means the first n records after initialization are all live, their times strictly increase from zero, and their times are strictly less than T. No condition is imposed on the next record. Further events before T are permitted. Once an appropriate process/count construction and almost-sure absence of ties are separately justified, this supports a first-n prefix or at-least-n-events-before-T interpretation. It does not directly describe EXACTLY n events before T. The missing final no-event condition and its terminal survival factor prevent that interpretation. No such final factor is hidden in m, q, A or B.

At points where an input ε(w,k)=0, the corresponding live waiting time is zero, and an otherwise live prefix with that repeated time fails the strict-order condition. These points are defined by the statement even though exponential inputs are positive almost surely. Equality of a time with T also fails B. There are no additional infinity checks on a terminal waiting time, cumulative count, or density. Infinity remains allowed for F and for nonnegative integrals; the total-density integral is nevertheless finite by the mass bound.

For n=0, H is the deterministic one-record live history (0,z₀), B=Ω for all T≥0, obs is the empty tuple, Prefix is a singleton, q=1, and the two history measures are the unit point mass at the initial history. This remains true at T=0. For n≥1 and T=0, B and Prefix are empty and the total mass is zero. Rank-zero E is permitted: rates vanish, positive thresholds have infinite waiting time, and n≥1 accepted histories have zero P-mass. A zero threshold can still give a finite zero-time record, but it fails strict ordering.

This is a finite-prefix theorem for every finite n. It contains no assertion of nonexplosion, existence of a continuous-time path for all times, stationarity or target invariance, exact event counting, expected event counts, query costs, or evolution to the horizon. There are no asymptotic or unnamed constants. α and β constrain V and η but do not enter the definitions independently.
